deviations.claim_in_article: “They enjoyed AI’s convenience, but a human was on the other end. They did not realize it.”
deviations.issue: The article states that users actually enjoyed the service and were unaware a human was handling the call. The Ledger establishes a lack of appropriate disclosure in the test, but does not establish users’ actual reactions or awareness.
deviations.explanation: It turns an illustrative possibility about users’ awareness into an asserted outcome not established by the Ledger; this implication is also present in the Japanese source.

deviations.claim_in_article: “human staff made inappropriate comments about race during calls. These calls were about trying to lower internet or cable fees.”
deviations.issue: The Ledger records one reported individual case involving an inappropriate race-related remark during a call. The article’s plural “comments” and “calls” can imply multiple instances, expanding that case.
deviations.explanation: Pluralizing the reported remark and call broadens the single reported case; the Japanese source refers to a remark and a call, so this expansion arises in translation/adaptation.
